tasting.narrative: This is the orthodox Glengoyne: a quarter-century exclusively in hand-selected sherry casks, coppery-red in the glass and trading on depth rather than weight. The nose stacks dried figs, raisins, rich chocolate and toffee pudding over red fruits, leather and brown sugar; WhiskyNotes (Ruben Luyten) adds jammy juicy figs and soaked cherries, plums, blackberries, espresso and burnt sugar from first-fill European-oak sherry. The palate follows with warm oak, fig, raisins, decadent chocolate, hazelnut and butterscotch, lifted by cinnamon, stewed fruit and a Seville-marmalade tang (The Whiskey Wash; corroborated by the distillery's own notes); Drinkhacker finds it nutty and savoury — toasted walnuts, coconut husks, vanilla sponge, milk chocolate and a tannic, nougat-and-Christmas-spice finish. The finish is very long, spicy liquorice slowly drying out. Crucially for an old sherried malt, the captured notes show no sulphur and no sharpness — this is clean sherry maturation on Scotland's slowest-distilled spirit, natural colour and non-chill-filtered at 48%. Pedigree is real and now multiply-sourced: The Whiskey Wash named it Best Scotch at its 2025 Awards (its founder: 'Scotch whisky doesn't get any better than this', corroborated by Master of Malt's blog), Drinkhacker an A- (~90), and the Whiskybase crowd 89.74/100 across 324 ratings. VERDICT: POUR — a benchmark, textbook old-school sherried Highlander to drink, not to chase as an investment; UK retail runs ~£420 (Master of Malt) to £525 (Royal Mile), £499 at the distillery, while the secondary average (~£250) sits below it. Keep its dried-fruit/chocolate sherry profile firmly separate from the citrus-and-vanilla White Oak 24.
